description: نحن فريق Mars Explorer، فريق شغوف بالعلوم والفضاء والتكنولوجيا، يجمعنا حب الاستكشاف والابتكار. نسعى إلى تحويل الأفكار الإبداعية إلى حلول تفاعلية تساعد على تبسيط المعلومات العلمية وجعل استكشاف الفضاء تجربة ممتعة ومفيدة للجميع. نؤمن بأن العمل الجماعي والتفكير الإبداعي هما أساس صناعة مستقبل أفضل.
summary: Mars Discoverers is an interactive platform designed to explore Mars by combining 2D maps and 3D models to provide an integrated scientific and educational experience. It allows users to explore different regions of the Martian surface and discover their coordinates, elevations, temperatures, atmospheric pressure, terrain, and mineral composition. The platform also enables users to compare two regions based on their geological and environmental characteristics and radiation protection levels. It presents information about the history of space missions and spacecraft involved in Mars exploration, including historical and current missions and rovers operating on its surface. The platform features an intelligent scientific assistant called ARES, powered by Google Gemini 2.5 Flash, which provides answers related to the selected location and supports both Arabic and English. It also includes a geological image analysis tool that evaluates the likelihood of an image being AI-generated, along with a fallback system that helps maintain essential functions when internet connectivity is weak. The platform supports voice interaction and is optimized for mobile phones and devices with limited capabilities. Mars Discoverers aims to make space science more accessible by transforming scientific data into an interactive experience that encourages learning, exploration, and a better understanding of Mars' natural resources, environmental conditions, and future human exploration possibilities.
details: Mars Discoverers – Project Details Mars Discoverers is a bilingual (Arabic and English) web-based planetary exploration and Geographic Information System (GIS) platform designed to make Mars exploration accessible through interactive scientific visualization, planetary data, and artificial intelligence. 1. Technologies and Development The application was developed using JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, and CSS3. Its backend runs on Node.js using a standalone server (server.cjs). Three.js and WebGL power the interactive 3D Mars globe and terrain visualization, while Leaflet.js provides the 2D mapping and GIS functionality. The application is hosted on Alwaysdata Linux Cloud with HTTPS support. 2. Planetary Exploration and Mapping Users can explore Mars through two synchronized interfaces: an interactive 3D globe and a 2D GIS map. The platform supports dynamic coordinate selection, allowing users to inspect different locations and access information about elevation, atmospheric pressure, temperature, mineral composition, and nearby Martian quadrangles. A terrain viewer also displays Digital Elevation Models (DEM), with adjustable vertical relief and wireframe visualization to help users understand the surface structure and elevation differences. 3. Scientific Analysis and Comparison The platform allows users to compare two Martian regions through comparative charts covering mineral composition, atmospheric conditions, radiation-related factors, and a Human Habitability Index. It also provides information about geological features, potential water ice resources, and locations relevant to future exploration. 4. Artificial Intelligence Integration ARES is an intelligent scientific copilot powered by Google Gemini 2.5 Flash through a secure server-side proxy. It receives contextual information about the selected region and answers scientific questions in Arabic or English. The platform also uses Gemini Vision API to analyze uploaded geological images and estimate the likelihood of AI-generated content. A local rule-based heuristic fallback provides responses to supported queries when internet connectivity is limited. 5. Voice Interaction and Accessibility Using the Web Speech API, the platform supports speech recognition and speech synthesis. Its bilingual interface provides Arabic and English content, RTL/LTR layouts, and mobile-friendly interaction to make planetary exploration more accessible. 6. Performance and Reliability The Node.js server uses native Gzip compression, caching headers, and a lightweight architecture to reduce data transfer and improve responsiveness. The application is designed to support devices with limited resources while maintaining essential functionality under unstable network conditions. 7. Factors Considered by the Team Our team considered several important factors while developing Mars Discoverers, including scientific accuracy, data reliability, accessibility, and ease of use. We focused on presenting complex scientific information about Mars in a simple and interactive way through 2D maps and 3D models. We also considered the importance of comparing Martian regions based on their geological and environmental characteristics, including temperature, atmospheric pressure, elevation, mineral composition, and radiation-related conditions. Accessibility was another key factor, so we included Arabic and English language support, voice interaction, and a mobile-friendly design. We also considered performance on devices with limited capabilities and maintaining essential functions under weak internet connectivity. Finally, we aimed to make the platform educational, informative, and useful for people interested in planetary science and future Mars exploration. 8. Innovation and Expected Impact Mars Discoverers combines 3D planetary visualization, GIS mapping, scientific data analysis, comparative analytics, and AI assistance in one accessible platform. Its goal is to simplify complex planetary datasets, encourage scientific learning, and support a better understanding of Martian geology, environmental conditions, natural resources, and the challenges of future human exploration. By bringing multiple exploration tools together, Mars Discoverers transforms planetary information into an interactive educational experience for students, researchers, and anyone interested in space exploration.
